Form cues are a coaching question, so here's what I'd work on. Stand with the bar over mid-foot, about hip-width stance, and grip just outside your legs. Before you pull, take the slack out of the bar: pull until you hear it click against the plates, chest up, lats tight as if you're squeezing oranges in your armpits. Then push the floor away with your legs instead of yanking with your back, and keep the bar dragging close to your shins and thighs the whole way. At the top, stand tall by squeezing your glutes, without leaning back.

The most common mistakes are the hips shooting up first, the bar drifting away from you, and rounding the upper back before the bar leaves the floor.

Tell me what "messed up" looks like for you, such as hips rising early, the bar swinging out, or a rounded back. I can then narrow it to the one or two cues that matter most. You can also send a video through form check and I'll open that screen for you.
